questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which OOP principle bundles data and methods operating on that data into a single unit while restricting direct access?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation binds data and code together into a class while hiding the internal object state from unauthorized external modification.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which mechanism allows a new class to inherit attributes and methods from an existing base class?
questions.explanation: Inheritance facilitates code reuse by allowing a derived class to inherit fields and behaviors from a base class.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is a special method automatically invoked when a new object instance is created?
questions.explanation: A constructor initializes a newly created object and prepares its state before use.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which OOP principle allows one interface to represent different implementations at runtime?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows a single method call to execute different derived-class implementations based on the runtime type.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What type of polymorphism is demonstrated by method overloading in C# and Java?
questions.explanation: Method overloading is resolved by the compiler at compile time based on parameter signatures, making it static polymorphism.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which keyword is used in C# to explicitly allow a method in a base class to be overridden by a derived class?
questions.explanation: The virtual keyword in C# indicates that a method, property, or event can be overridden in any derived class using the override keyword.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: In the SOLID design principles, what does the "L" stand for?
questions.explanation: The Liskov Substitution Principle states that objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of a subclass without altering program correctness.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is the relationship between an Engine and a Car called when the Engine cannot exist without the Car?
questions.explanation: Composition represents a strict part-of relationship where the child component has no independent lifecycle outside its parent.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which access modifier allows members to be accessed within the same class and any derived classes, but not outside?
questions.explanation: The protected access modifier restricts access to the containing class and types derived from the containing class.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What lookup mechanism does the runtime engine use to resolve virtual method calls in C++ and C#?
questions.explanation: Virtual calls use a vtable (virtual method table) containing pointers to the dynamic implementation of virtual functions for each class.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What issue arises when a class inherits from two classes that both inherit from the same common base class?
questions.explanation: The Diamond Problem occurs in multiple inheritance when ambiguity arises regarding which parent implementation of a base method to inherit.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which design pattern ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it?
questions.explanation: The Singleton pattern restricts class instantiation to a single object instance and manages global state access.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which keyword prevents a class from being inherited in C#?
questions.explanation: The sealed keyword prevents other classes from inheriting from it in C# (equivalent to final in Java).

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is an abstract class in object-oriented programming?
options: A class that cannot be instantiated directly and is meant to be subclassed
A class containing only static methods
A class compiled into machine code
questions.explanation: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly and serves as a blueprint containing abstract and/or concrete methods for subclasses.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: In the Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP), high-level modules should depend on what?
questions.explanation: DIP states that high-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions (interfaces).

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What does a class define in OOP?
options: A blueprint or template for creating objects
questions.explanation: A class is a user-defined blueprint from which individual objects with state and behavior are instantiated.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which pattern defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable?
questions.explanation: The Strategy pattern enables selecting an algorithm at runtime by encapsulating each algorithm into its own interchangeable class.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is the Open/Closed Principle in SOLID software design?
options: Classes should be open for modification, closed for extension
Classes should be open for extension, but closed for modification
APIs should be open source and closed to commercial use
Classes must have open public fields and closed private methods
questions.explanation: Software entities should be open for extension (adding new behavior) but closed for modification of existing tested source code.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is the core component of an Operating System that manages system resources and hardware interaction?
questions.explanation: The kernel is the central component of an OS, responsible for memory management, process control, and direct hardware communication.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is a process in an operating system?
questions.explanation: A process is an active program in execution, with its own address space, program counter, and system resources.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm assigns each process a fixed time slice in cyclical order?
questions.explanation: Round Robin allocates a fixed quantum (time slice) to each runnable process in circular queue sequence.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What condition occurs when two or more processes are blocked indefinitely waiting for each other to release resources?
questions.explanation: A deadlock occurs when processes hold resources and wait for others held by conflicting processes in a circular wait.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which algorithm is used for deadlock avoidance by verifying whether resource allocation leads to a safe state?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra Banker algorithm simulates resource allocation to ensure the system never enters an unsafe deadlock-prone state.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is the phenomenon where the OS spends more time swapping virtual memory pages than executing instructions?
questions.explanation: Thrashing happens when the working set of processes exceeds physical memory, causing continuous page faults and disk swapping.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What mechanism allows a CPU to immediately respond to high-priority hardware signals?
questions.explanation: An interrupt signals the CPU to suspend current execution and run an Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) immediately.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is the primary difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads within the same process share the same memory address space
questions.explanation: Threads are lightweight execution units within a process that share the same address space and open file descriptors.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?
options: To cache virtual-to-physical page table address translations
questions.explanation: The TLB is a high-speed hardware cache in the MMU that stores recent virtual-to-physical address mappings to avoid memory latency.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which synchronization primitive is an integer variable accessed only through wait() and signal() operations?
questions.explanation: A semaphore is an atomic integer counter used to synchronize access to shared resources via P (wait) and V (signal) operations.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Coffman four necessary conditions for a deadlock?
questions.explanation: The four Coffman conditions are Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait. Priority inversion is a scheduling anomaly.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which system call in Unix/Linux creates a new child process by duplicating the existing calling process?
questions.explanation: The fork() system call duplicates the calling process, creating an exact child process with a new unique PID.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What type of fragmentation occurs when allocated memory blocks have unused space internal to the allocated partition?
questions.explanation: Internal fragmentation occurs when allocated fixed-size memory blocks are larger than requested, leaving wasted space inside.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: In virtual memory systems, what is the working set of a process?
options: The entire program binary loaded into RAM
The set of pages referenced by the process during a recent sliding time window
The CPU registers saved on a context switch
questions.explanation: The working set model identifies the set of memory pages actively referenced by a process during a sliding time window.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which CPU mode allows execution of privileged instructions and direct hardware access?
questions.explanation: Kernel mode (Ring 0) provides unrestricted access to physical hardware instructions and kernel address space.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What page replacement algorithm replaces the page that has not been used for the longest period of time?
questions.explanation: LRU keeps track of page usage over time and evicts the page that has not been referenced for the longest duration.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is priority inversion and how is it solved in real-time operating systems?
options: A low-priority task preempts a high-priority task; solved via Round Robin
A medium-priority task preempts a low-priority task holding a resource needed by a high-priority task; solved via Priority Inheritance
A process has its priority set to zero; solved via nice()
Threads deadlock over mutexes; solved via kill()
questions.explanation: Priority inversion is solved using Priority Inheritance Protocol, where the lower task temporarily inherits the high task priority.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What data structure does the OS use to track information about an active process (state, PC, registers, memory limits)?
questions.explanation: The Process Control Block (PCB) contains state details, CPU registers, scheduling priority, and memory pointers for a process.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What does SQL stand for?
questions.explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, the standardized domain-specific language for relational database management.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which column constraint uniquely identifies each record in a database table?
questions.explanation: A Primary Key uniquely identifies each row in a database table and cannot contain NULL values.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: In the ACID transaction properties, what does the "I" guarantee?
questions.explanation: Isolation ensures concurrent transactions execute without interfering with each other intermediate states.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which normal form eliminates partial functional dependencies on a composite primary key?
questions.explanation: 2NF requires a table to be in 1NF and ensure all non-key attributes are fully functionally dependent on the primary key.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which data structure is most widely used by relational database engines for table indexing on disk?
questions.explanation: B+ Trees have high fan-out, shallow depth, and linked leaf nodes, making them optimal for disk I/O and range scans.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter records resulting from a GROUP BY aggregation?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters aggregated groups produced by GROUP BY, whereas WHERE filters individual rows before grouping.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What type of JOIN returns all records from the left table and matched records from the right table?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched values from the right table, filling nulls if no match.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What phenomenon occurs when a transaction reads rows, and another transaction inserts new rows matching the query condition before commit?
questions.explanation: Phantom Read occurs when re-executing a range query reveals new rows inserted and committed by a concurrent transaction.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which SQL command is used to remove all records from a table without logging individual row deletions?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE deallocates data pages directly, making it much faster than DELETE while preserving table schema.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What does the Two-Phase Locking (2PL) protocol guarantee in database concurrency control?
questions.explanation: Strict 2PL ensures conflict serializability by dividing lock handling into an expanding growing phase and shrinking phase.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which normal form eliminates transitive functional dependencies between non-key attributes?
questions.explanation: Third Normal Form (3NF) requires 2NF and mandates that non-key attributes depend only directly on the primary key.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which ACID property guarantees that all operations within a transaction succeed together or all rollback?
questions.explanation: Atomicity ensures that a transaction is all-or-nothing: if any step fails, the entire transaction rolls back.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What is write-ahead logging (WAL) in database crash recovery?
options: Writing query logs to disk before compilation
Ensuring log records are written to persistent storage before database pages are flushed
Writing to replica nodes before primary
questions.explanation: WAL ensures transaction log records describing updates are persisted to non-volatile disk before dirty data pages are written.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which SQL command changes existing data values in database tables?
questions.explanation: The UPDATE statement modifies existing data values in one or more columns within a database table.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What is a Foreign Key in relational database design?
options: A key imported from an external database server
A column referencing the Primary Key of another table
An index that cannot be modified
questions.explanation: A Foreign Key is a field in one table that uniquely identifies a row in another table, enforcing referential integrity.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: In the CAP theorem for distributed databases, what three properties cannot all be simultaneously guaranteed during a partition?
questions.explanation: The CAP theorem states that a distributed data store can only simultaneously guarantee at most two of: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which keyword eliminates duplicate rows from an SQL SELECT result set?
questions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT filters duplicate rows from the final result set, returning only unique records.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What is a database View?
options: A physical copy of table data stored in RAM
A virtual table based on the result-set of an SQL query
A graphical user interface for table design
An audit log of user queries
questions.explanation: A View is a virtual table that presents the dynamic result of a stored SQL query without storing duplicated data itself.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: How many layers are in the OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) reference model?
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What protocol resolves human-friendly domain names (e.g. google.com) into numerical IP addresses?
questions.explanation: Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses for routing.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the standard three-way handshake sequence used to establish a TCP connection?
questions.explanation: TCP initiates connections via a 3-way handshake: Client sends SYN, server replies SYN-ACK, client sends ACK.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the default port number for secure HTTPS traffic?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses standard port 443 (HTTP uses port 80; SSH uses port 22).

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address to its physical MAC hardware address on a local network?
questions.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps an IP network layer address to a physical MAC link layer address.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the size of an IPv4 address and an IPv6 address, respectively?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits (4 bytes) long; IPv6 addresses are 128 bits (16 bytes) long.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What mechanism does TCP use to detect and recover from lost packets without waiting for retransmission timeout?
questions.explanation: Fast Retransmit retransmits a missing segment immediately when receiving three duplicate ACKs before timeout expires.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which Transport Layer protocol is connectionless and prioritizes low latency over guaranteed delivery?
questions.explanation: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is connectionless, non-guaranteed, and has low overhead, ideal for real-time gaming and VoIP.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which routing protocol is an exterior gateway protocol that coordinates routing decisions across the global Internet autonomous systems?
questions.explanation: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is the standardized exterior path-vector protocol that routes traffic between Autonomous Systems.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What protocol automatically assigns dynamic IP addresses, default gateways, and DNS servers to host devices on a LAN?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) automatically assigns IP configuration to devices joining a network.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What does CIDR subnet mask /24 represent in terms of usable host IP addresses?
questions.explanation: A /24 subnet has 2^(32-24) = 256 addresses; subtracting network (0) and broadcast (255) leaves 254 usable host addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the purpose of the SYN Cookie mechanism in network security?
options: To store HTTP login session state
To defend web servers against TCP SYN flood denial-of-service attacks
questions.explanation: SYN Cookies encode connection state into the initial sequence number, preventing server resource exhaustion during SYN floods.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which utility uses ICMP echo requests to verify connectivity and measure round-trip latency to a destination host?
questions.explanation: ping sends ICMP Echo Request packets and awaits Echo Reply to verify reachability and latency.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What does Network Address Translation (NAT) accomplish?
options: Enables multiple private IP devices on a LAN to share a single public IP address
questions.explanation: NAT maps private local IP addresses to a public routable IP address, conserving IPv4 address space.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) standard size on standard Ethernet frames?
questions.explanation: Standard Ethernet MTU is 1500 bytes; packets larger than this must be fragmented unless Jumbo Frames (9000 bytes) are enabled.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: At which OSI layer does a network Router operate?
questions.explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network Layer), inspecting IP packets to determine optimal path routing.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption in SSL/TLS?
options: Symmetric uses one shared key; asymmetric uses a public/private key pair
Asymmetric is used for bulk data transfer
questions.explanation: Symmetric uses a shared secret for fast data encryption; asymmetric uses public/private keys for initial key exchange.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: In Distance Vector routing protocols, what issue does Split Horizon and Poison Reverse help prevent?
questions.explanation: Split Horizon prevents routing loops by prohibiting a router from advertising a learned route back onto the interface it came from.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST, each comparison cuts the search space in half, resulting in logarithmic O(log n) time complexity.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which data structure operates on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order?
questions.explanation: A Stack operates on a LIFO discipline where elements pushed last are popped first.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort when pivot selection is poor?
questions.explanation: QuickSort degrades to quadratic O(n^2) worst-case time when partitions are highly unbalanced (e.g. sorted array with extreme pivot).

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which algorithm finds the single-source shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra algorithm uses a priority queue (min-heap) to compute shortest paths from a source to all nodes in non-negative graphs.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which algorithm can find shortest paths in graphs that contain negative edge weights (and detect negative cycles)?
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford relaxes all edges |V|-1 times and can detect negative-weight cycles by checking if further relaxation is possible.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of insertion and retrieval in a Hash Table with a good hash function?
questions.explanation: Hash tables achieve constant O(1) average lookup and insert times by computing an array index directly from the key hash.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which graph traversal algorithm explores nodes level by level using a Queue data structure?
questions.explanation: BFS visits neighbor nodes layer by layer using a FIFO Queue, guaranteeing shortest path in unweighted graphs.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the balance factor of a node in an AVL tree allowed to be for it to remain balanced?
questions.explanation: In an AVL tree, the height difference (balance factor) between left and right subtrees of every node must be -1, 0, or +1.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What algorithmic paradigm solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing results (memoization)?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Programming stores answers to overlapping subproblems in a lookup table to avoid redundant exponential computation.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the time complexity of building a Binary Heap of n elements using the bottom-up Heapify approach?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up heap construction (Floyd build-heap) runs in linear O(n) time, as mathematical summation of heights converges to O(n).

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has a guaranteed worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and is stable?
questions.explanation: MergeSort guarantees O(n log n) in all cases (best, average, worst) and maintains the relative order of equal elements (stable).

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the space complexity of Depth-First Search (DFS) on a tree of height h?
questions.explanation: DFS requires memory proportional to the maximum depth of the recursion stack, which is bounded by tree height O(h).

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which data structure efficiently supports finding the Minimum Spanning Tree using Disjoint Set Union (DSU / Union-Find)?
questions.explanation: Kruskal sorts all edges and uses DSU with union-by-rank and path compression to detect cycles in nearly O(alpha(V)) time.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: In a circular queue implemented using an array of size N, what condition indicates the queue is full?
questions.explanation: A circular queue with one empty slot reserved is full when (rear + 1) % N == front.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which tree traversal visits the nodes in order: Left Subtree, Root, Right Subtree?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits Left -> Root -> Right, which produces elements in ascending sorted order for a BST.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the amortized time complexity of the find operation in Union-Find with path compression and rank optimization?
questions.explanation: Path compression and union-by-rank achieve an amortized bound of O(alpha(n)), the inverse Ackermann function, which is practically <= 4.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: What is the time complexity to insert an element at the beginning of a Singly Linked List with a head pointer?
questions.explanation: Inserting at head simply updates the new node next pointer to point to head and reassigns head, executing in O(1) time.

questions.subject: Data Structures and Algorithms
questions.question: Which data structure is typically used to implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache in O(1) time for all operations?
options: Hash Map and Doubly Linked List
questions.explanation: A Hash Map paired with a Doubly Linked List provides O(1) key lookups and O(1) node detachment and head insertion.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: Which software development methodology emphasizes short iterative sprints, daily standups, and adaptive planning?
questions.explanation: Scrum is an Agile framework where teams deliver working increments of software in 1 to 4 week iterations called sprints.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What type of software testing validates that individual units or methods work correctly in isolation?
questions.explanation: Unit testing verifies that smallest testable pieces of source code (methods/functions) function correctly in isolation.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What testing technique re-runs existing tests to ensure recent code changes have not broken existing working features?
questions.explanation: Regression testing validates that bug fixes or feature additions do not inadvertently break existing functionalities.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What does CI/CD stand for in modern DevOps practice?
questions.explanation: CI/CD automates building, testing, and deploying software updates continuously and reliably.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: In Git version control, what does git rebase do compared to git merge?
options: Re-applies commits from one branch onto the tip of another, creating a linear history
Creates an extra merge commit combining branches
Pushes code to origin without confirmation
questions.explanation: git rebase replays commits on top of another branch tip, producing a clean, linear project history without merge commits.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What Git command creates a new working branch and switches to it in one step?
questions.explanation: git checkout -b <name> (or git switch -c <name>) creates and switches to a new branch in a single command.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Code Review in professional software development?
options: To identify defects, improve code quality, and share knowledge across the team
To compile code on the server
questions.explanation: Code reviews catch defects early, enforce architectural standards, and promote team-wide knowledge sharing.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What is technical debt in software engineering?
options: The implied cost of future rework caused by choosing an easy, fast solution over a better design
questions.explanation: Technical debt describes the cumulative cost of future maintenance and refactoring incurred by expedient sub-optimal choices.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: In the Test-Driven Development (TDD) cycle, what is the sequence of steps?
questions.explanation: TDD follows the Red-Green-Refactor loop: write a failing test first, write minimum code to pass it, then refactor cleanly.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What architectural style structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services communicating via lightweight APIs?
questions.explanation: Microservices decouple domain capabilities into independently scalable, deployable services communicating over HTTP/gRPC.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: Which document outlines the requirements and functional specifications agreed upon by stakeholders and engineers?
questions.explanation: An SRS document formally details the functional and non-functional requirements of a software system.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What type of testing evaluates how a software application behaves under extreme and peak traffic workloads?
questions.explanation: Load and stress testing assesses stability, throughput, and error rates when the system is subjected to high concurrent loads.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What is cyclomatic complexity in software metrics?
options: Number of lines of code in a file
Quantitative measure of the number of linearly independent paths through program source code
questions.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity (M = E - N + 2P) measures the decision logic paths, indicating testing and maintenance complexity.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What does DRY stand for in software engineering best practices?
questions.explanation: Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY) promotes reducing code duplication and centralizing business logic in single sources of truth.

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.question: What is the purpose of Semantic Versioning (SemVer: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)?
options: Communicating breaking changes (MAJOR), new features (MINOR), and bug fixes (PATCH)
questions.explanation: SemVer standardizes version increments: MAJOR for incompatible API changes, MINOR for backwards-compatible additions, PATCH for fixes.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: Which HTTP status code indicates a successful request?
questions.explanation: HTTP 200 OK signifies that the server received, understood, and successfully processed the client request.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What does CSS stand for in web technology?
questions.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) defines the visual presentation, styling, and layout of HTML documents.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: In RESTful APIs, which HTTP verb is idempotent and used to update or replace an existing resource?
questions.explanation: PUT replaces an entire resource and is idempotent, meaning executing multiple identical PUT requests produces the same result.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What mechanism prevents a malicious website from making unauthorized API requests to another domain using the user browser credentials?
questions.explanation: The Same-Origin Policy and CORS enforce security boundaries preventing unauthorized cross-origin data access.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: How does JavaScript single-threaded concurrency model handle asynchronous I/O and promises?
options: The Event Loop with Task Queue and Microtask Queue
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses an Event Loop where microtasks (Promises) and macrotasks (setTimeout, I/O) are processed on a single main thread.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: Which JavaScript keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const declares an immutable binding (block-scoped variable identifier that cannot be reassigned).

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What is JSON Web Token (JWT) typically used for in modern web architectures?
options: Stateless user authentication and secure claims transmission
questions.explanation: JWT encodes cryptographically signed JSON payloads containing user identity claims, enabling stateless authentication.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What security vulnerability occurs when user input is rendered into a webpage without proper sanitization, executing malicious JavaScript?
questions.explanation: XSS vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject malicious client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Document Object Model (DOM) in web browsers?
options: An object-oriented tree representation of the structured HTML document
To manage cookies on the hard drive
questions.explanation: The DOM represents the HTML document as a node tree that programming languages like JavaScript can manipulate dynamically.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What header flag prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing session cookies, mitigating session hijacking via XSS?
questions.explanation: The HttpOnly flag directs browsers to block document.cookie access to the cookie, protecting it from theft via XSS.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: Which HTML5 element is used to draw graphics and animations on the fly via scripting?
questions.explanation: The <canvas> element provides a resolution-dependent bitmap canvas used for 2D/3D graphics via JavaScript.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What is a closure in programming languages like JavaScript and Python?
options: A function bundled with references to its surrounding lexical environment
A closed class that cannot be inherited
A private variable scope in HTML
questions.explanation: A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical state.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What technique in single-page applications (SPAs) renders pages on the server initially before hydrating on the client?
questions.explanation: SSR generates the HTML for initial page requests on the server, improving Time-to-First-Byte (TTFB) and SEO indexing.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What format does JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) use to store data?
questions.explanation: JSON is a lightweight, human-readable data interchange text format composed of key-value pairs and arrays.

questions.subject: Web Development and Programming
questions.question: What full-duplex communication protocol enables continuous, persistent two-way communication over a single TCP connection between browser and server?
questions.explanation: WebSocket provides persistent, low-latency, full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which access modifier restricts member access strictly to within the same class?
questions.explanation: The 'private' access modifier hides members from external classes and subclasses, ensuring strict encapsulation.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is the term for defining multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists in the same class?
questions.explanation: Method overloading is compile-time polymorphism where methods share a name but differ in parameter count or types.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which keyword is commonly used in derived classes to refer to the immediate base class constructor or members?
questions.explanation: 'base' (in C#) or 'super' (in Java) refers to the parent/base class members or constructor.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Can an abstract class be instantiated directly using the 'new' keyword?
options: No, it must be inherited by a concrete class
Only if it has no abstract methods
questions.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be directly instantiated; they define a blueprint that concrete subclasses must implement.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is the relationship described by class Dog inheriting from class Animal?
questions.explanation: Inheritance represents an IS-A relationship, meaning a Dog is an Animal.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which design principle states that software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification?
questions.explanation: The Open/Closed Principle (OCP) encourages writing code that can be extended with new behavior without modifying existing code.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: In C#, what keyword must be added to a base class method to allow a derived class to override it?
questions.explanation: In C#, methods must be declared as 'virtual' (or 'abstract') in the base class to enable overriding via 'override' in subclasses.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What is the difference between an Interface and an Abstract Class?
options: A class can implement multiple interfaces, but typically inherit only one base class
Abstract classes cannot contain concrete methods
questions.explanation: Most single-inheritance languages permit inheriting one base class while implementing multiple interfaces.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: Which design pattern ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it?
questions.explanation: The Singleton pattern restricts class instantiation to a single shared instance throughout the application lifecycle.

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: What problem occurs when a derived class strengthens preconditions or weakens postconditions compared to its base class?
questions.explanation: LSP requires that subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering correctness (preconditions cannot be strengthened).

questions.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questions.question: In runtime polymorphism with virtual tables (vtable), what overhead is typically incurred?
options: Extra pointer indirection per object and vtable lookup per virtual call
questions.explanation: Virtual method dispatch involves an extra vtable pointer (vptr) per object and a table dereference at runtime.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What data structure does the operating system use to store state, program counter, and registers for each process?
questions.explanation: The PCB holds essential context for process management, including CPU registers, PID, priority, and memory pointers.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads within the same process share the same memory address space
questions.explanation: Threads share their parent process's code, data, and heap, but maintain independent stacks and register sets.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What state does a process transition to when it issues a blocking I/O request?
questions.explanation: When waiting for an external event such as disk or network I/O, the scheduler moves the process to the Waiting/Blocked state.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which scheduling algorithm assigns the CPU to processes in strict arrival order?
questions.explanation: FCFS (FIFO) is a non-preemptive scheduler that executes processes in the order they join the ready queue.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary Coffman conditions for a deadlock to occur?
questions.explanation: The four Coffman conditions are Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is 'Thrashing' in virtual memory management?
options: Excessive disk paging activity where the system spends more time swapping pages than executing
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the active working sets of processes exceed physical RAM, causing constant page faults.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What algorithm uses safety checks with allocation, max, and available matrices to avoid deadlocks?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's Banker's Algorithm tests for safe resource allocation states to prevent deadlocks.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What hardware component translates virtual page addresses into physical frame numbers?
questions.explanation: The MMU performs virtual-to-physical address translation, frequently aided by the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB).

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: In the context of the Dining Philosophers problem, how can deadlock be prevented while retaining concurrency?
options: Enforcing an asymmetric rule: odd philosophers pick left fork first, even philosophers pick right first
questions.explanation: Breaking the symmetry (e.g. odd/even resource ordering) eliminates the circular wait condition, preventing deadlock.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question: What is Belady's Anomaly in page replacement algorithms?
options: FIFO can yield more page faults when allocated more physical page frames
questions.explanation: Belady's Anomaly is the counterintuitive phenomenon where increasing frame count increases page faults in FIFO.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for end-to-end reliable data delivery and port multiplexing?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4, e.g. TCP/UDP) provides host-to-host process communication using port numbers.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which protocol resolves a human-readable domain name (like www.google.com) into an IP address?
questions.explanation: Domain Name System (DNS) maps human-readable domain names to numeric IP addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the standard port number for unencrypted HTTP web traffic?
questions.explanation: Port 80 is the default port for HTTP, while port 443 is used for HTTPS.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which protocol is connectionless and does not guarantee packet delivery or order?
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) provides lightweight, connectionless datagram transmission without retransmissions.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What sequence of packets completes the standard TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: A TCP connection is established by the client sending SYN, the server responding with SYN-ACK, and client acknowledging with ACK.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: How many usable host IP addresses are available in an IPv4 subnet with prefix /28?
questions.explanation: A /28 subnet has 32 - 28 = 4 host bits. 2^4 = 16 total IPs minus 2 (network and broadcast) = 14 usable hosts.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: Which protocol resolves an IP address to a local physical MAC address on an Ethernet LAN?
questions.explanation: ARP broadcasts a query on the local link to find the Layer 2 MAC address matching an IPv4 address.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What is the primary function of Network Address Translation (NAT)?
options: Mapping private RFC 1918 IP addresses to public routable IP addresses
questions.explanation: NAT allows multiple devices in a private LAN to share one or more public IPv4 addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: In TCP congestion control, what triggers entering the Fast Recovery phase rather than Slow Start?
questions.explanation: Three duplicate ACKs indicate packet loss while packets continue flowing, prompting Fast Retransmit / Fast Recovery.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.question: What mechanism does Distance Vector routing use to prevent the Count-to-Infinity problem?
questions.explanation: Split Horizon prevents a router from advertising a route back out the same interface through which it was learned.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which SQL command is used to extract data from a relational database table?
questions.explanation: SELECT is the fundamental SQL DML query statement used to retrieve rows from tables.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What is an attribute (or combination of attributes) that uniquely identifies each tuple in a relation called?
questions.explanation: A Primary Key uniquely identifies every record in a table and cannot contain NULL values.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which constraint enforces referential integrity between two relational tables?
questions.explanation: A Foreign Key establishes a relationship with a Primary Key in another table to maintain referential integrity.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: In ACID properties, what does 'A' stand for?
questions.explanation: Atomicity guarantees that all operations in a transaction succeed together, or all are aborted and rolled back.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What normal form requires that a relation be in 1NF and have NO partial functional dependencies on candidate keys?
questions.explanation: 2NF requires eliminating partial dependencies where a non-prime attribute depends on only part of a composite key.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table, and matching rows from the right table (filling with NULL if no match)?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN (or LEFT OUTER JOIN) includes all records from the left relation, matched or unmatched.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What is the primary trade-off of adding multiple indexes to a heavily written database table?
options: Speeds up SELECT queries but slows down INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations
questions.explanation: Indexes accelerate read queries via B-Trees, but every write modification must also update the index structures.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Which transaction isolation level prevents Dirty Reads but still allows Non-Repeatable Reads?
questions.explanation: Read Committed ensures only committed changes are read, preventing dirty reads; repeatable read prevents non-repeatable reads.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: Under Two-Phase Locking (2PL), what occurs during the shrinking phase?
options: Locks can only be released; no new locks may be acquired
questions.explanation: In 2PL, once a transaction releases any lock (shrinking phase), it cannot acquire any new locks, ensuring conflict serializability.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.question: What concurrency phenomenon occurs when Transaction 1 reads a set of rows satisfying a condition, Transaction 2 inserts a row matching that condition, and Transaction 1 re-reads and discovers the new row?
questions.explanation: A Phantom Read occurs when newly inserted or deleted rows appear in subsequent queries within the same transaction.
